name: Sitarjevec Mine
zag_role: Characterisation of mine ochre as a pigment
description: ZAG characterised the yellow limonite mud that forms in the mine and assessed it as a source of natural pigment for artistic and textile use. The work is an example of the institute's materials side rather than its structures side.
history: Sitarjevec is a polymetallic mine on the hill above Litija that worked lead and mercury ores and later zinc, copper, iron bearing material and barite, the choice following market demand and price. Mining on the hill goes back to prehistory, the earliest written evidence is the 1537 gravestone of the mining master Cristof Bruckherschmidt, and a smelter operated from 1881. Work stopped at the end of July 1965 because the remaining ore was too poor, the recovery technology outdated and silicosis widespread among the miners, and the adits were then blasted shut. After 2000 limonite speleothems were discovered in the abandoned workings, iron and manganese formations regarded as among the finest in Europe, some of which grow up to 5 cm a year. The municipality rehabilitated part of the mine between 2017 and 2019, creating 632 m of museum routes, and guided tours began in December 2017 with the Glavni rov opening on 22 April 2021.
